pr_title: fix: improve error handling for malformed csv parsing
pr_body:
Fixes #11019.

This pull request introduces two checks to enhance error handling when parsing CSV files, particularly in cases where quote characters are improperly placed:

1. **Global Scope Check (File-Level):** We now verify that the count of quote characters is even at the global, whole-file scope. An odd count of quote characters signifies a malformed CSV. Escaping a quote is achieved by doubling it (e.g., "ab""cd""de") and so the contract is upheld.
2. **Local Scope Check (Field-Level):** We examine the last character in each field, ensuring that it is a quote character. Additionally we confirm that the field length is at least 2 bytes. This prevents situations where a field consists solely of a quote character. This check is performed if the first byte of a field is a quote character.

Both tests are performed only if `quote_char == Some(x)`.

The checks improve an error handling when trying to parse csv like:
```
a,b,c
A,"B,C
```  
or:
```
a,b,c
A,"B,"C  
```
pr_comments: I don't think the way to do this is by adding a pass over the entire file just to count the number of quote characters. This could read gigabytes of data.
This is indeed way too expensive. Error's are allowed to do some compute, but they can be catched and handled and should not cause the huge wall times.

Maybe only performing the second check is the way. This option is more efficient since it examines the last byte (unless it's escaped) of fields that have already been iterated. This check can handle situations like the one mentioned in the issue. While skipping the first check might allow some corner cases, I don't see a more performance-friendly approach without making significant changes to existing structures.

issue_context.title: Segfault reading invalid CSV
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

Create a CSV called `temp_test.csv` (which is intentionally created to mimic a failed file transfer partway through the transfer):
```csv
"WellCompletionCWI","FacilityID","ProductionMonth","ReportedHoursProdInj","ProdAccountingProductType","ReportedVolume","VolumetricActivityType"
"SK0000608V001","SK BT B1H3780","202001","","GAS","1.700","PROD"
"SK0127960V000","SK BT 0018977","202001","","GAS","45.500","PROD"
"SK0127960V000","SK BT 0018977","
```

```python
df = pl.read_csv(
  'temp_test.csv',
  infer_schema_length=10_000_000_000_000,
  dtypes={'ProductionMonth': pl.Utf8, 'ReportedHoursProdInj': pl.Int16, 'ReportedVolume': pl.Float64},
)
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

Even though the CSV file is invalid (due to a failed file transfer), it should not cause Polars to outright crash. Instead, an error message should be displayed or similar. 

As it is, this may even represent a security vulnerability if it's possible to craft a CSV file that causes it to crash in a certain way.

### Expected behavior

Some sort of error should occur, in the same way that pandas throws an error on this same test file.

It also appears to raise an exception without the `dtypes`:
```python
pl.read_csv(b"""
"WellCompletionCWI","FacilityID","ProductionMonth","ReportedHoursProdInj","ProdAccountingProductType","ReportedVolume","VolumetricActivityType"
"SK0000608V001","SK BT B1H3780","202001","","GAS","1.700","PROD"
"SK0127960V000","SK BT 0018977","202001","","GAS","45.500","PROD"
"SK0127960V000","SK BT 0018977","
""".strip()
)
# thread '<unnamed>' panicked at /Users/user/git/polars/crates/polars-io/src/csv/buffer.rs:87:23:
# slice index starts at 1 but ends at 0
# PanicException: slice index starts at 1 but ends at 0
```
Probably the same underlying issue, but may be useful for debugging.
Thanks for the way shorter repro! Sorry I had a bit extra in there earlier

I believe the culprit lies in the single quotation mark at the end of the last line.  This led Polars to infer that it should be wrapped in double quotes(i.e. `needs_escaping`), but in fact, it did not.

The cause of the problem is here: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/d7411e0160a9e38b10ba26843590efa9b4067792/crates/polars-io/src/csv/utils.rs#L664 or if you want to look at it from the other side: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/d7411e0160a9e38b10ba26843590efa9b4067792/crates/polars-io/src/csv/buffer.rs#L203-L206 [escape_field's contract](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/d7411e0160a9e38b10ba26843590efa9b4067792/crates/polars-io/src/csv/utils.rs#L657-L659) specifies that _bytes_ has to end with a quote character but it does not require for it to have a a minimum length of 2. And so it tries to index "1..0".
A potential solution to address this issue can be implemented in the [caller's code](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/d7411e0160a9e38b10ba26843590efa9b4067792/crates/polars-io/src/csv/buffer.rs#L203-L206), by introducing a simple check like the following: ``` let bytes_len = bytes.len(); if bytes_len == 1 || bytes[bytes_len -1] != self.quote_char { polars_bail!(ComputeError: "invalid utf-8 sequence"); } ```
With this change, the application will panic with a more descriptive error message: ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "/a/polars/py-polars/csv.py", line 3, in a = pl.read_csv(b""" ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/a/polars/py-polars/polars/io/csv/functions.py", line 364, in read_csv df = pl.DataFrame._read_csv( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/a/polars/py-polars/polars/dataframe/frame.py", line 768, in _read_csv self._df = PyDataFrame.read_csv( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ exceptions.ComputeError: Could not parse `"` as dtype `str` at column 'ProductionMonth' (column number 3). The current offset in the file is 307 bytes. You might want to try: - increasing `infer_schema_length` (e.g. `infer_schema_length=10000`), - specifying correct dtype with the `dtypes` argument - setting `ignore_errors` to `True`, - adding `"` to the `null_values` list. ```

review_comments: I don't want an extra branch in the hot loop. This will slow down parsing well formed csv files.

I don't want this. This does a whole scan of the file.

The csv-parser is designed to be fast for correct files. This isn't a csv-file sanitizer.
